summary: Announces which link numbers may be used on the ARPANET. Link numbers 2 through 71 can be used for connections, 0 is the control link, others are reserved, and 191 is for measurement work. It updates RFC 107 and was written into the Host-Host protocol document.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC assigns uses to ranges of Host-Host link numbers. It identifies the control link, links for connections, reserved links, and links for measurement or private experiments.

subtitle: A table assigning link numbers for control, connections and experiments.

tldr.problem: Hosts needed a shared statement of which Host-Host link numbers were available for connections.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns link 0 to control, links 2 through 71 to connections, and other ranges to reserved or experimental uses.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 107 and says the assignments will appear in the Host-Host Protocol document then being written.

sections.title: The Assignment Announcement
sections.content:
Alex McKenzie announces that link numbers 2 through 71, inclusive, are valid for connections. He says the assignments will be included in the Host-Host Protocol document he is writing.

The unit metadata says RFC 179 updates RFC 107.
sections.plainLanguage: The note announces which link numbers hosts can use for connections. It says the same assignments will be included in a protocol document.

sections.title: Link Number Ranges
sections.content:
Link 0 is the control link. Links 2 through 71 are available for connections. Link 1 and links 72 through 190 are reserved and not for current use.

Link 191 is reserved for measurement work under the direction of the Network Measurement Center at UCLA. Links 192 through 255 are available for private experimental use.
sections.plainLanguage: Link 0 carries control information, and links 2 through 71 are for connections. Other ranges are reserved for measurement or private experiments.

sections.title: Scope of the Table
sections.content: The RFC presents a link-number table without a longer explanation of why each range was selected. It is a short assignment notice, and its metadata records that it updates RFC 107.
sections.plainLanguage: This document gives the assignments rather than a detailed design explanation. It updates RFC 107.
